originality.rationale: The historical SFS computation formula is fully acknowledged as prior art. The narrow novelty assessment is the explicit all-parameter comparison law for swapping unequal-length intact demographic epochs, its sharp opposite-sign region and universal accumulated-hazard threshold. No equivalent comparative theorem was found in inspected published-finding corpus records and primary work; historical priority is provisional and general rearrangement results remain a risk.
residual_risks: Pre-existing general variable-size SFS formulas algebraically evaluate both compared histories; additional published inequalities could directly subsume the stated sign theorem.
Historical priority has not been independently established across all literature, including non-indexed classical coalescent rearrangement results.

value.rationale: A complete sharp, non-numerical sign classification for a natural genetic-demography comparison: SFS components can move in opposite directions under mere reordering of identical historical epochs. The universal cutoff in pre-swap cumulative hazard and unique duration-scale transition explain when such reversal can occur; three sequences is sharp. A model-level interpretation is offered without unwarranted empirical inference claims.
